description: A looping sample player with a granular layer: a bank of onboard loops out of the box, through-zero varispeed, and grains from the whole loop down to 15ms

params.text: Chooses which loop of the bank plays, named on the display above it
Sets the playback speed, from twice backwards through stopped at the centre of its travel to twice forwards; pitch follows speed as it would on tape
Sets the grain length, from the whole loop played straight through at the bottom down to 15ms at the top
Raises the grain overlap from single grains up to an eight-deep lattice
Offsets where in the loop the grains are drawn from
Adds random scatter to the grain positions and spreads them across the stereo field
Sets the output level, up to twice unity at the top
Steps on to the next loop in the bank
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the jack beside it before it is added to the control it belongs to

inputs.text: A rising edge steps on to the next loop in the bank; it reads high above 1V and low below 0.1V
Moves the playback speed, 10V covering the knob's whole range, scaled by the trimmer beside it
Moves the grain length, 10V sweeping its whole range, scaled by the trimmer beside it
Moves the grain overlap, 10V sweeping its whole range, scaled by the trimmer beside it
Moves where in the loop grains are drawn from, 10V sweeping its whole range, scaled by the trimmer beside it
Moves the position scatter and stereo spread, 10V sweeping its whole range, scaled by the trimmer beside it

outputs.text: The left channel out, ±5V; with the right output unpatched this jack carries the two channels summed to mono
A 1ms trigger at 10V each time the loop wraps round

notes: it plays without any patching: the onboard bank of loops is loaded when the module is added
the display names the loop in play and traces a playhead across it, and clicking it steps on to the next loop
the red splice marker orbiting the speed knob moves with the loop, lengthening its trail as the speed rises and running backwards below zero
a loaded folder is read under fixed limits, 99 files, 60 seconds a file and 192MB a bank, held as 16-bit, so a folder of stems cannot fill memory
menu: Load sample folder (.wav)... — swaps the onboard loops for a folder of WAV files of your own, for this module alone
Restore onboard litany — throws away the loaded folder and goes back to the bundled loops
